card.name: Just before a governor or viceroy title
card.fires_on: Small words or punctuation (the, his, our, an opening bracket, a comma) right before an expected official title such as governor, viceroy or admiral. Seen in historical text about colonial or royal rule.

modes.label: Before a ruler's representative
modes.description: A small word or bracket precedes a title for someone who governs on a king's behalf.
modes.example: In 1474 L was the seat of the king's representative<< (>>the Woiwoda).

modes.label: After appointment verbs
modes.description: A word right after a verb of appointing or directing, where an office name comes next.
modes.example: After the fall of Montreal in 1760, he was<< named>> its military governor.

modes.label: Before viceroy or similar
modes.description: A possessive or article before a viceroy or admiral.
modes.example: directed<< his>> viceroy Barreto to draw

card.writes: It pushes the next word toward governing and government terms such as govern, governing and Gover-.
card.plain: It fires on little words just before a title like governor or viceroy is expected in historical text.
